_meta.comment: Curated installable model catalog used by the Settings UI and the installer wizard. LLMs ship in Phase 5; image models are flagged for Phase 6 (Image Studio); video models for Phase 7 (Video Lab); NVIDIA SANA family landed in v1.1.0 Phase 12. Ollama-sourced entries delegate digest verification to `ollama pull` and carry no sha256. Hugging Face entries carry a per-model `weights` manifest (v1.8.0 Phase 3): an explicit file list, each downloaded from https://huggingface.co/{repo}/resolve/main/{path} into <models_root>/weights/<model-id>/{path} (models_root defaults to ~/.nexus/models) -- the per-model directory the diffusion runtime loads at startup (diffusers from_pretrained on the model directory; repo-relative subpaths like transformer/ are preserved). Each file pins a SHA-256 (versions.lock.json discipline): all-zero digests are placeholders -- the installer's weights puller warns, skips verification, and logs the computed digest; rotate pins with scripts/installer/build/pin-hf-weights.py. source.sha256 remains the primary-blob digest for older consumers and is superseded by weights.files[].sha256. v1.8.0 Phase 4 adds the selection-UX fields: `task` (chat | agentic | image | video | audio | embed) drives the installer's catalog sections; `strengths` / `whyRecommended` / `differentiators` carry the per-model copy the wizard cards render; `provenance` records publisher + lineage for curated entries (required on uncensored ones). Uncensored entries (uncensored: true) were curated 2026-07-03 with license + provenance verified per entry; per-VRAM-tier defaults live in recommended.json. v1.9.0 Phase 4 adds the scannable-catalog metadata: `origin` (publisher country, or Community) and `agentic` (agentic-coding capability flag -- set on the Gemma 4 family + the coding specialists so both surface in the installer's Agentic tab); an optional `guardrails` string overrides the installer's derived Uncensored/Safety-tuned/N/A label. The audio pillar (type/task `audio`) is curated: speech (faster-whisper STT MIT, Kokoro + Piper TTS) and generation (MusicGen CC-BY-NC-4.0, Stable Audio Open community-license) -- STT/TTS are permissive + CPU-capable and default on every tier; the non-commercial generation models are listed opt-in (never defaults). v1.14.0 Phase 1 curation: releaseDate (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) is now a first-class field on every selectable model, rendered as a card pill by the installer picker; gated open-weight opt-ins (svd, stable-audio-open-1.0, sana-1.6b-int4) carry requiresLicense=true + licenseUrl so the installer guided Hugging Face step (accept license + free token) can unlock them, and sd1.5 was re-pointed from the withdrawn runwayml repo to the public stable-diffusion-v1-5 mirror; auxiliary types (vae, controlnet) stay excluded from the picker by the loader; the per-family best-fit collapse (show the single best variant that fits the detected hardware, larger tiers grayed) happens in the installer picker at render time, so the catalog stays a complete data source for the desktop app and diffusion runtime. v1.18.0 Phase 3 adds optional toolCallingVerified + toolCallingBenchmark (OW-A4) and MoE activeParams/totalParams in billions (LG-A3); omitted fields stay unverified / dense. v1.19.0 Phase 1 adds LFM2.5-2.6B as the low-VRAM Agentic entry (official Liquid GGUF via the Ollama hf.co bridge -- the official Ollama library does not carry it at curation time -- plus a real SHA-256 pin on weights.files) and an optional licenseNote use-restriction string so ungated licenses with a commercial-use cap stay visible without triggering requiresLicense gated-auth. Record contextWindow conservatively at 32K until Phase 2 verifies the 128K claim.

models.name: gemma4
models.description: Google's Gemma 4 E2B is a compact 2B-parameter chat model from the USA. The smallest chat tier: it stays responsive on a 4 GB GPU, or even with no dedicated GPU at all.
strengths: Fast everyday chat and quick questions
Summarizing short documents and drafting notes
Runs acceptably with no dedicated GPU at all
models.whyRecommended: The only chat tier that stays responsive without a dedicated GPU, so every machine gets a working assistant.
models.differentiators: Smallest download of the chat family (1.6 GB); trades reasoning depth for speed and reach.

strengths: General conversation, drafting, and rewriting
Reliable instruction following for its size
Loads fast and leaves VRAM headroom on 8 GB cards
models.whyRecommended: Best chat quality per gigabyte on mainstream gaming GPUs; the default most users should start with.
models.differentiators: The sweet spot of the Gemma 4 ladder: near-instant loads at 2.7 GB with noticeably better answers than the 2B tier.

models.description: Google's Gemma 4 26B is a larger chat model from the USA for 18 GB+ GPUs. Upper-mid tier: deeper reasoning and longer documents than the E-series.
strengths: Nuanced multi-step reasoning
Long-document comprehension and synthesis
MoE routing keeps generation fast for its quality class
models.differentiators: Mixture-of-experts: 26B-class answers while activating only a fraction of the parameters per token.

toolCallingBenchmark.result: pass: in-repo agentic=true (coding-engine / installer Agentic tab); not a live golden-task A/B

models.name: gemma4
models.description: Google's Gemma 4 31B is the flagship local chat model from the USA. The strongest answer quality in the catalog, on a single 24 GB GPU.
strengths: Complex reasoning and analysis
High-fidelity long-form writing
Best factual grounding of the Gemma family
models.whyRecommended: The strongest local chat quality that fits a single 24 GB GPU.
models.differentiators: Dense 31B weights: maximum quality per prompt, no expert-routing variance.

toolCallingBenchmark.result: pass: in-repo agentic=true (coding-engine / installer Agentic tab); not a live golden-task A/B

models.name: gemma4
models.description: Google's Gemma 4 12B is a mid-size chat model from the USA that also understands images. It reads book-length material in one go and runs on 12 GB VRAM and up.
strengths: Multimodal input: text and images in one chat
256K context window for whole-project or book-length material
Mid-tier quality that fits a 12 GB GPU
models.whyRecommended: Multimodal input and a 256K context window at a size that fits 12 GB GPUs.
models.differentiators: Native image input with a 256K context; pulled from the Ollama library so it registers and loads reliably on a Gemma-4-capable Ollama.

toolCallingBenchmark.result: pass: in-repo agentic=true (coding-engine / installer Agentic tab); not a live golden-task A/B

models.name: llama3.1
models.description: Meta's Llama 3.1 8B is a well-rounded chat model from the USA. A dependable alternative with the broadest fine-tune and tooling ecosystem of any open model its size.
strengths: Balanced general-purpose chat
Huge community ecosystem of fine-tunes and guides
128K context window
models.differentiators: The most widely deployed open 8B: predictable behavior and the broadest third-party compatibility.

models.name: llama3.1
models.description: Meta's Llama 3.1 70B is a workstation-class chat model from the USA. Near-frontier reasoning fully offline, but it needs 40 GB+ of VRAM or aggressive CPU offload.
strengths: Frontier-adjacent reasoning fully offline
Strong coding and math for a chat generalist
128K context window
models.differentiators: The largest chat option in the catalog; for multi-GPU or unified-memory workstations only.

models.name: qwen2.5
models.description: Alibaba's Qwen 2.5 7B is a multilingual chat model from China. A strong non-English alternative with good math and structured-output skills on a 7-8 GB GPU.
strengths: Strong multilingual coverage (29+ languages)
Good at JSON and structured output
Solid math for a 7B model
models.differentiators: The multilingual pick of the 7-8 GB class; noticeably better non-English answers than same-size peers.

models.name: qwen2.5
models.description: Alibaba's Qwen 2.5 14B is a mid-size multilingual chat model from China for 12 GB GPUs. Deeper reasoning than the 7B, with the same multilingual strengths.
strengths: Multilingual chat with deeper reasoning than the 7B
Reliable structured output at scale
Fits 12 GB cards comfortably
models.differentiators: Scales the Qwen multilingual strengths to the 12 GB tier under a permissive Apache-2.0 license.

models.name: qwen2.5-coder
models.description: Alibaba's Qwen 2.5 Coder 7B is a code-specialized model from China. Built for the Coding pillar: generation, repair, and editor completions across 40+ languages.
strengths: Code generation and bug fixing across 40+ languages
Fill-in-the-middle for inline editor completions
Tool-calling for agentic coding workflows
models.whyRecommended: The most capable agentic-coding model that fits 8 GB cards, and it still runs CPU-only in a pinch.
models.differentiators: Purpose-trained on code: outperforms general-purpose 7B chat models on coding benchmarks by a wide margin.

toolCallingBenchmark.result: pass: in-repo agentic=true (coding-engine / installer Agentic tab); not a live golden-task A/B

models.name: qwen2.5-coder
models.description: Alibaba's Qwen 2.5 Coder 14B is a mid-tier coding model from China that still fits 12 GB GPUs. Stronger multi-file reasoning and refactoring than the 7B.
strengths: Multi-file refactoring and cross-module reasoning
More reliable tool-calling in long agent loops
Better test generation and code review than the 7B tier
models.whyRecommended: Meaningfully stronger multi-file agentic work than the 7B tier while still fitting a 12 GB GPU.
models.differentiators: The best coding quality per VRAM in the 12 GB class; Apache-2.0 licensed.

toolCallingBenchmark.result: pass: in-repo agentic=true (coding-engine / installer Agentic tab); not a live golden-task A/B

models.name: deepseek-coder-v2
models.description: DeepSeek's Coder V2 16B is an advanced coding model from China with fast inference on 14 GB+ GPUs. Near-flagship coding skill for the Agentic tier.
strengths: Top-of-catalog code generation and repair quality
Fast generation: only 2.4B parameters active per token
Strong on math-heavy and algorithmic code
models.whyRecommended: Top agentic quality in the catalog: mixture-of-experts delivers near-flagship coding skill at consumer-GPU speeds.
models.differentiators: MoE architecture: 16B-class quality with the per-token cost of a 2.4B model.

toolCallingBenchmark.result: pass: in-repo agentic=true (coding-engine / installer Agentic tab); not a live golden-task A/B

models.name: lfm2.5
models.description: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-2.6B is a 2.6B-parameter agentic model from the USA. It is designed for on-device planning, tool calling, and multi-step tasks. The Q4_K_M GGUF is 1.67 GB and stays responsive on a 3 GB GPU, or even with no dedicated GPU at all. Context is recorded as 32K pending Phase 2 empirical verification of the 128K claim.
strengths: Tool-calling agentic workflows on CPU-only or sub-4 GB machines
Multi-step planning at a 1.67 GB download
Dedicated Agentic-tab pick below the 7B coder floor
models.whyRecommended: The only dedicated agentic (tool-calling) catalog entry that fits CPU-only hosts and sub-4 GB GPUs.
models.differentiators: Fills the sub-4 GB agentic gap: Q4_K_M GGUF at 1.67 GB, CPU-capable, with an LFM Open License v1.0 commercial-use cap (see the license note). Context length is recorded conservatively at 32K until Phase 2 verifies the 128K claim.
models.licenseNote: Apache-2.0-based, royalty-free. Fine-tunes may stay proprietary. Free commercial use is limited to entities under USD 10M annual revenue; a commercial license is required above that. Qualified non-profits are exempt. This is a use restriction, not a download gate.
models.provenance: Official Liquid AI GGUF, Q4_K_M, ungated Hugging Face repo LiquidAI/LFM2.5-2.6B-GGUF. Pulled at install time from the official repo via Ollama's hf.co bridge; Nexus does not redistribute weights.

models.name: nomic-embed-text
models.description: Nomic AI's Nomic Embed Text is a small embedding model from the USA, not a chat model. It powers the semantic memory layer: search, recall, and retrieval across your conversations and files.
strengths: Semantic search over conversations and documents
Long-context retrieval (8K tokens per passage)
Tiny footprint: 0.27 GB, runs on any hardware
models.whyRecommended: Required by the semantic memory layer; tiny and runs anywhere, so it ships in every default selection.
models.differentiators: The only embedding model in the catalog; without it, memory search falls back to keyword matching.

models.name: sdxl-turbo
models.description: Stability AI's SDXL Turbo is a speed-tuned image model from the UK that draws in 1-4 steps. The fast-draft pick of the SDXL lineage, ideal for rapid prompt iteration.
strengths: Near-real-time drafts: 1-4 denoising steps
Good for rapid prompt iteration
Full SDXL ecosystem compatibility
models.differentiators: Fastest SDXL variant in the catalog; quality ceiling below the fine-tuned checkpoints.

models.name: sdxl-base
models.description: Stability AI's Stable Diffusion XL 1.0 is the reference image model from the UK. The compatibility baseline for the SDXL LoRA and ControlNet ecosystem.
strengths: Broadest LoRA and ControlNet compatibility
Well-documented, predictable prompting
Strong general-purpose 1024px generation
models.differentiators: The unmodified SDXL reference: fine-tunes beat it on looks, nothing beats it on ecosystem compatibility.

models.name: juggernaut-xl
models.description: Juggernaut XL v9 is a photorealistic image model from the USA: a community fine-tune of SDXL by KandooAI and RunDiffusion with no built-in content filter. The uncensored photorealism default for 8-12 GB GPUs.
strengths: Best-in-class photorealistic people and scenes
Uncensored weights: no baked-in content filter
Works with the whole SDXL LoRA/ControlNet ecosystem
models.whyRecommended: The proven photorealism workhorse of the SDXL family, with uncensored weights and a clearly documented license.
models.differentiators: One of the most-downloaded SDXL fine-tunes ever (6M+ downloads); markedly more lifelike output than SDXL base at the same VRAM cost.
models.provenance: Community SDXL 1.0 fine-tune co-developed by KandooAI and RunDiffusion; published at huggingface.co/RunDiffusion/Juggernaut-XL-v9 (RunDiffusionPhoto v2 blend). Uncensored basis: photoreal training data and no safety filter in the weights. License verified 2026-07-03 from the HF model card.
models.license: CreativeML Open RAIL-M (no paid-API redeployment without a RunDiffusion license)

models.name: realvisxl
models.description: RealVisXL V5.0 is a photorealistic image model from the open-source community: a fine-tune of SDXL by SG161222 with no built-in content filter. The uncensored photorealism default for 16 GB+ GPUs.
strengths: Exceptional skin texture, lighting, and fine detail
Uncensored weights: no baked-in content filter
Strong prompt adherence for a photoreal fine-tune
models.whyRecommended: The sharpest photoreal detail of the SDXL fine-tune class; uncensored weights under a standard OpenRAIL++ license.
models.differentiators: Tuned for maximum realism rather than speed; pairs well with higher step counts on 16 GB+ cards.
models.provenance: Community SDXL 1.0 fine-tune by SG161222; published at huggingface.co/SG161222/RealVisXL_V5.0 (fp16 checkpoint). Uncensored basis: photoreal training data and no safety filter in the weights. License verified 2026-07-03 from the HF model card.

models.name: flux
models.description: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.1 Schnell is a large image model from Germany that generates in just 4 steps. The prompt-adherence flagship for 24 GB GPUs, with the best text rendering in the catalog.
strengths: Best prompt adherence and text rendering in the catalog
4-step generation despite its size
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.differentiators: A different architecture class than SDXL: dramatically better at complex compositions and legible text, at 3x the download size.

models.name: sd1
models.description: Stable Diffusion 1.5 is the classic lightweight image model from the UK. The lightest in the catalog: 512px generation on 4 GB VRAM, with a vast legacy fine-tune ecosystem.
strengths: Runs on 4 GB VRAM
Enormous legacy LoRA and checkpoint ecosystem
Fast at 512px
models.differentiators: The compatibility floor: lowest quality of the image catalog, but runs where nothing else fits.

models.name: ltx-video
models.description: Lightricks' LTX-Video is a speed-focused text-to-video model from Israel for 12 GB+ GPUs. The fastest clip generation in the catalog, with good motion on short clips.
strengths: Fastest clip generation in the catalog
Good motion coherence for short clips
Text-to-video and image-to-video in one model
models.differentiators: The speed pick: generates a clip in seconds where diffusion peers take minutes.

models.name: wan2.1-t2v
models.description: Alibaba's Wan 2.1 T2V is a 1.3B text-to-video model from China that runs on ~8 GB VRAM at 480p, with no built-in content filter. The consumer-hardware entry point for local video.
strengths: Runs on ~8 GB consumer GPUs (480p)
Leading VBench motion quality in the small-model class
Uncensored-capable: no weights-level content filter
models.whyRecommended: The best open video model that fits consumer 8-16 GB GPUs, under a fully permissive Apache-2.0 license.
models.differentiators: The consumer-hardware entry point for local video: where LTX-Video optimizes speed, Wan 2.1 optimizes quality per GB of VRAM.
models.provenance: Published by Alibaba (Wan-AI) at huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B; original release, not a fine-tune. Uncensored basis: no safety filter in the released weights (content filtering in the hosted service is pipeline-level). License verified 2026-07-03 from the HF model card.

models.name: wan2.2-ti2v
models.description: Alibaba's Wan 2.2 TI2V is a 5B text-and-image-to-video model from China that reaches 720p at 24 fps on a single 24 GB card, with no built-in content filter. The higher-resolution local-video default.
strengths: 720p @ 24 fps on a single 24 GB GPU
Text-to-video and image-to-video in one model
Uncensored-capable: no weights-level content filter
models.whyRecommended: The strongest local video quality that fits a single 24 GB GPU, under a fully permissive Apache-2.0 license.
models.differentiators: The high-compression Wan2.2-VAE makes true 720p24 practical on one consumer card; among the fastest 720p open models.
models.provenance: Published by Alibaba (Wan-AI) at huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B; original release, not a fine-tune. Uncensored basis: no safety filter in the released weights (content filtering in the hosted service is pipeline-level). License verified 2026-07-03 from the HF model card.

models.name: stable-video-diffusion
models.description: Stability AI's Stable Video Diffusion 1.1 is an image-to-video model from the UK. It animates a still image into a short clip with coherent camera motion.
strengths: Animates existing images with coherent camera motion
Predictable, stable short clips
Well-documented reference pipeline
models.differentiators: Image-to-video specialist: give it a picture, not a prompt.
models.gatedReason: Access-gated open-weight model (HTTP 401 for unauthenticated clients): the installer guided Hugging Face step (accept the model license on its page, then sign in with a free read token) unlocks it. Public alternatives (ltx-video, wan2.2-ti2v-5b) also cover image-to-video.

models.name: sana
models.description: NVIDIA's SANA 1.5 1.6B is an efficient 1024px image model from the USA. About 2x faster than SDXL Turbo on 6 GB VRAM, with permissive Apache-2.0 weights.
strengths: Very fast 1024px generation on 6 GB VRAM
Strong text rendering for its size
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.whyRecommended: The efficiency pick: full 1024px quality on GPUs that cannot fit the SDXL-class models.
models.differentiators: Linear-attention architecture: SDXL-class output at a fraction of the compute and VRAM.

models.name: sana-sprint
models.description: NVIDIA's SANA Sprint is a one-step image model from the USA. The speed tier behind Image Studio's Fast Preview toggle, at the same 6 GB footprint as SANA 1.5.
strengths: Single-step generation: instant previews
Same 6 GB VRAM footprint as SANA 1.5
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.differentiators: One denoising step: the fastest image entry in the catalog, tuned for previews over final quality.

models.name: sana
models.description: NVIDIA's SANA 1.6B 2K is a high-resolution image model from the USA for 12 GB GPUs. Native 2048px generation on the efficient SANA core.
strengths: Native 2048px generation
Same efficient linear-attention core as SANA 1.5
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.differentiators: The 2K step of the SANA resolution ladder.

models.name: sana
models.description: NVIDIA's SANA 1.6B 4K is an ultra-high-resolution image model from the USA for 20 GB GPUs. Native 4096px, poster-scale output without upscalers.
strengths: Native 4096px generation
Poster-scale output without upscalers
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.differentiators: The only native-4K image entry in the catalog.

models.name: sana
models.description: NVIDIA's SANA 1.5 1.6B INT4 is a compressed image model from the USA that fits 5 GB GPUs. The low-VRAM way to still get 1024px generation (needs the nunchaku runtime).
strengths: Smallest capable 1024px model (1.4 GB, 5 GB VRAM)
INT4 quantization with minimal quality loss
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.differentiators: The low-VRAM safety net of the image catalog; needs the nunchaku runtime dependency.
models.gatedReason: Access-gated open-weight model (HTTP 401) that also needs the nunchaku runtime dependency: the installer guided Hugging Face step unlocks the download and the diffusion runtime provides nunchaku. The public sana-1.6b-1024 covers 1024px generation without either requirement.

models.name: dc-ae
models.description: MIT HAN Lab Deep Compression AutoEncoder (32x compression, 32 channels). Auto-loaded by every SANA pipeline.

models.name: sana-controlnet
models.description: Pose-conditioning ControlNet for SANA. Pairs with the OpenPose preprocessor (controlnet_aux).

models.name: sana-controlnet
models.description: Depth-conditioning ControlNet for SANA. Pairs with the MiDaS preprocessor (controlnet_aux).

models.name: sana-controlnet
models.description: Canny-edge-conditioning ControlNet for SANA. Pairs with the OpenCV Canny preprocessor.

models.name: sana-video
models.description: NVIDIA's SANA-Video 2B is a fast 720p text-to-video model from the USA for 12 GB GPUs. The efficiency pick: faster than the Wan family, higher fidelity than LTX-Video.
strengths: Fast 720p clips on 12 GB VRAM
Efficient linear-attention video architecture
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.differentiators: The efficiency pick for 720p: faster than the Wan family, higher fidelity than LTX-Video.

models.name: faster-whisper-large-v3
models.description: OpenAI's Whisper Large v3 (Faster-Whisper build) is a speech-to-text model from the USA that runs on CPU or GPU. Accurate transcription and translation across 90+ languages, on any hardware.
strengths: Accurate multilingual speech-to-text (90+ languages)
4-5x faster than reference Whisper via CTranslate2
Runs on CPU -- no GPU required
models.whyRecommended: The de-facto local speech-to-text model: accurate, multilingual, and fast enough to run without a GPU.
models.differentiators: MIT-licensed and CPU-capable, so every install gets working transcription regardless of hardware.

models.name: kokoro-82m
models.description: Kokoro 82M is a tiny open-weight text-to-speech model from the open-source community, with natural, expressive voices. Fast and CPU-friendly at just 0.35 GB.
strengths: Natural, expressive speech synthesis
Only 82M parameters -- runs on CPU in real time
Apache-2.0: fully permissive license
models.whyRecommended: The best-quality local text-to-speech that still runs on CPU, under a fully permissive license.
models.differentiators: Punches far above its 0.35 GB size; the go-to open TTS model for local, offline voice.

models.name: piper-en-us-lessac
models.description: Piper is a fast on-device text-to-speech system from the open-source community; this is the US-English Lessac (medium) voice. Low-latency speech even on a Raspberry Pi-class CPU.
strengths: Extremely fast, low-latency on-device TTS
Tiny footprint: runs on a Raspberry Pi-class CPU
Dozens of voices and languages available
models.differentiators: The lightest TTS option in the catalog; optimized for embedded and low-power hardware rather than maximum expressiveness.

models.name: musicgen-medium
models.description: Meta's MusicGen Medium is a 1.5B text-to-music model from the USA that turns a prompt into short instrumental clips. Opt-in rather than a default: it needs a GPU and ships under a non-commercial license.
strengths: Text-to-music generation from a prompt
Coherent melody and instrumentation for short clips
Single-stage autoregressive model
models.differentiators: The music-generation pillar of the audio catalog; needs a GPU and ships under a non-commercial license, so it is opt-in rather than a default.

models.name: stable-audio-open
models.description: Stability AI's Stable Audio Open is a text-to-audio model from the UK for sound effects and short musical samples (up to ~47s). Opt-in under a community license; the sound-design counterpart to MusicGen.
strengths: Text-to-audio: sound effects and musical samples
Generates variable-length stereo audio
Strong for foley and instrument one-shots
models.differentiators: The sound-design counterpart to MusicGen; tuned for samples and effects rather than full songs. GPU-gated, opt-in (community license).
models.gatedReason: Access-gated open-weight model (HTTP 401 for unauthenticated clients): the installer guided Hugging Face step (accept the model license on its page, then sign in with a free read token) unlocks it. MusicGen Medium is a public alternative for music generation.

models.name: rapidocr
models.description: RapidOCR PP-OCRv4 is a community-maintained ONNX text-detection and text-recognition pair that reads images and PDFs on any machine. It runs on the CPU through ONNX Runtime, so document parsing works on Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), and Linux with no GPU at all.
strengths: Runs on CPU -- no GPU required, works on every supported OS
Tiny download (about 20 MB) and fast to load
Apache-2.0 across both the models and the runtime
models.whyRecommended: The portable half of the document-OCR pair: every install gets working document parsing regardless of hardware, mirroring how faster-whisper guarantees transcription everywhere.
models.differentiators: Traditional detect-then-recognize OCR rather than a vision-language model: far smaller and CPU-capable, at the cost of layout reasoning on complex documents.

models.name: unlimited-ocr
models.description: Baidu's Unlimited-OCR is a 3B vision-language model from China that parses a whole multi-page document in one pass, preserving layout and structure as markdown. It is CUDA-first: the publisher documents NVIDIA GPUs only, so Nexus offers it exclusively on capable NVIDIA hosts and falls back to RapidOCR everywhere else.
strengths: One-shot long-horizon parsing of multi-page PDFs (32K context)
Layout-aware markdown output, not just loose text lines
MIT-licensed open weights
models.whyRecommended: The quality tier for document parsing: a vision-language model reads tables, columns, and headings that a detect-then-recognize engine flattens.
models.differentiators: Understands document structure rather than only locating text, at the cost of a 3B GPU-resident model and NVIDIA-only support.
models.provenance: Published by Baidu on Hugging Face as baidu/Unlimited-OCR; open weights under MIT with model-specific inference code in the repository.
models.guardrails: N/A -- document parsing model, no generation guardrails apply
